title: Policy engine: compatibility guardrails for quantization profiles + safe fallback
author: Ravi Menon
release_notes: Adds deterministic compatibility evaluation for route-level quantization profiles (model family, GPU SKU class, and max context constraints). Incompatible profiles now fall back to baseline precision with explicit reason codes + metrics; enabling incompatible profiles returns actionable validation errors (when called via config validation path).
description: Motivation: Route-level quantization profile enablement must be safe-by-default. This PR adds compatibility evaluation inside the policy engine so that any resolved quantization profile ref is deterministically accepted/rejected based on (a) model family/variant constraints, (b) GPU SKU class support, and (c) max context / sequence-length regime constraints. When a profile is incompatible, policy resolution falls back to baseline precision (i.e., quantization disabled) and emits explicit metrics/loggable reason codes; default behavior is unchanged when quantization is not enabled on the route. Scope: This change is in the control-plane policy resolution path (routing policy engine), not runtime kernel selection. The runtime still receives a resolved decision (apply profile X vs baseline). Design notes: (1) Determinism: compatibility evaluation uses only stable inputs available at policy time (route config + resolved model_id/model_variant + deployment hardware class + requested max_tokens/context caps) and does not depend on live capacity state. (2) Explicit reason codes: on fallback, policy attaches a `quant_profile_resolution_outcome` and `quant_profile_incompat_reason` to the resolved route policy result; downstream components can tag logs/traces with the resolved outcome. (3) Safety: Incompatibility results in fallback to baseline precision rather than hard failure; the only hard failure is for malformed/unknown profile refs during config validation (used by Console preview). (4) Guardrails: GPU support is expressed as coarse SKU classes (e.g., `nvidia_a10`, `nvidia_l4`, `nvidia_a100`, `nvidia_h100`) to avoid per-SKU churn; max context constraints enforce `profile.max_context_tokens >= route.max_context_tokens` and optionally a stricter cap for mixed-precision kernels. (5) Observability: adds counters for fallback rate by reason and a gauge for enabled routes (as seen by policy evaluation). Implementation details: - Adds `QuantProfileCompatibilityEvaluator` with pure functions and table-driven rules. - Adds normalization layer mapping fleet GPU identifiers to `GpuSkuClass` used by policy. - Implements compatibility checks: model family match (e.g., `llama3` profile cannot be applied to `mistral`), variant allowlist (some profiles are `*-instruct` only), GPU SKU class membership, and max context token ceilings. - Adds safe fallback: if `route.quantization_profile_ref` resolves but is incompatible, policy returns baseline quantization mode and sets `quant_profile_applied=false` plus reason. - Adds config validation endpoint support hook: when called in "validate" mode, returns structured error messages (used by Console to show warnings/errors before save). - Adds metrics: `policy_quant_profile_fallback_total{reason=...}` and `policy_quant_profile_applied_total` plus debug logging at INFO with route_id + model_id + profile_id + reason. Tests: - Unit tests: table-driven cases across families, GPU classes, and context limits. - Property test: compatibility evaluation is stable across input ordering and is idempotent. - Integration-ish policy tests: route config with ref -> policy resolution -> expected outcome + metrics tags. Related work: - Route config field added in PR #18411. - Control plane endpoints in PR #18445 (consumes this evaluator during preview/validation). Follow-ups: - Consider expanding GPU class mapping for private/on-prem SKU reporting. - Once runtime emits `quant_profile_id` in traces, add dashboard panels broken down by `resolution_outcome` + `reason` (tracked in ENG-5817).
commits: policy: add GPU sku class normalization for hosted/dedicated fleets
policy: enforce max context constraints and mixed-precision caps
observability: emit fallback/applied counters with stable tags
tests: table-driven compatibility coverage + determinism/idempotence checks
docs (internal): update policy engine notes for quant profile fallback behavior
conversation: Jordan Lee (review): Can we guarantee the fallback decision is deterministic if `gpu_type` is missing in some private deployments? If so, what do we do when class is unknown?

Ravi Menon (author): Yep. Added explicit `GpuSkuClass.UNKNOWN` mapping. If unknown, we treat profile as incompatible unless the profile explicitly lists `unknown_ok=true` (not present in v1), so we will fallback to baseline with reason `gpu_class_unknown`. This keeps behavior stable/safe for private deployments that don’t report SKU class yet.
Ethan Park (review): I like the reason codes. Can we ensure tags are bounded? Please avoid putting raw model_id/profile_id in metric labels.
Ravi Menon (author): Agreed. Metrics only tag `reason` and `outcome`. Route/model/profile identifiers are log fields only (structured logs) and will be trace annotations downstream.
Mina Haddad (review): For context constraints: are we comparing against request-time context or route max context? Request-time may vary.

Ravi Menon (author): We compare against the effective route cap that routing enforces (`route.max_context_tokens` + `max_output_tokens`). That’s what we can evaluate deterministically at policy time. Runtime still has its own internal guards, but this should prevent the most common misconfig.
Noah Patel (review): Can we add a dedicated reason for ‘profile supports fp8 acts but hardware class only supports int8’? I want to differentiate in dashboards.
Ravi Menon (author): Added `precision_path_unsupported` with a submessage in logs (not a metric tag) indicating which path failed. Metric tags remain bounded.
Naomi Feldman (review): Please confirm this does not change default behavior when quantization is off. Also, validation errors vs fallback behavior should be clear for audit/compliance.

Ravi Menon (author): Confirmed. When route has `quantization_profile_ref=default/none`, evaluator is not invoked. When ref is set, runtime behavior is either apply profile or fallback to baseline; config validation returns hard error only in validate/preview mode (Console), not in live request routing.
Connor O'Brien (review): Add a brief note in the runbook about new fallback reason codes so oncall can interpret spikes. Doesn’t need to block merge but would be good.
Ravi Menon (author): Added a short section to internal policy doc; runbook update tracked in ENG-5817/ENG-5819 workstreams.
